## Soft Metadata

> [!WARNING]
> **Tier 2 (community estimate)** — Soft Metadata below adapted from publisher-disclosed practices (acamh.onlinelibrary.wiley.com author guide) and community-aggregator evidence (editage.com) gathered 2026-05. See [SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md](../../../../SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md) for the Skeleton → Tier 2 → Tier 1 lifecycle.

> **The core value of this entry.** OpenAlex cannot fill any of these — they require lived experience and community knowledge. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../../../CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidance.

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | High — ACAMH (Association for Child & Adolescent Mental Health) is internationally oriented |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | Medium — accepts non-Western data within medical-research framework |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | High — child mental health diversity, neurodiversity, family-structure papers regularly published |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | Child and adolescent psychiatry + clinical-developmental research — child/adolescent psychosocial development (2,367 articles), autism research (1,099), ADHD (968), family/disability support (598), child abuse/trauma (520) per OpenAlex |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes (strong)
- **If yes, what kind?** Manuscripts must demonstrate **clinical / mechanism contribution to child or adolescent psychiatry**. Editorial assignment to 1 of 8 decision editors specializing in subject domain — domain fit is structural.
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Active triage culture — ~50% rejected without review (often within first week). Total acceptance rate ~18%. Getting past the first-week triage is a structural signal.

### Methodological Preferences

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 5 | Core method |
| Qualitative interviews | 2 | Accepted with mixed-methods or clinical-narrative framing |
| Autoethnography | 1 | Rare |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | Accepted with clinical-mechanism focus |
| Mixed methods | 4 | Common in child-psychiatry research |
| Meta-analysis | 5 | Welcomed; PRISMA reporting expected |
| Treatment / Intervention | 5 | Distinctive strength |

### Voice & Style

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **First-person voice acceptance (0-5)** | 1 — formal academic register |
| **Expected density** | Almost none |
| **Writing style notes** | Wiley clinical-research format; child-psychiatry vocabulary; DSM-5-TR / ICD-11 diagnostic terminology; CONSORT-style reporting for trials |

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

Reviewers drawn primarily from the child and adolescent psychiatry community — ACAMH-affiliated faculty and senior clinicians. Editorial assignment to 1 of 8 decision editors specializing in subject domain (autism, ADHD, mood disorders, trauma, neurodevelopmental, etc.). Active triage culture: ~50% rejected without review, often within first week. Decision in ~5 weeks (excluding desk rejects). Common reviewer demands: "Clinical significance?", "Mechanism specificity?", "Data availability?".

| Aspect | Detail | Evidence |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Dominant tradition** | Child + adolescent psychiatry researchers | https://acamh.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/hub/journal/14697610/forauthors.html |
| **Reviewer competence variance** | Low-Medium — domain-editor matching reduces variance |
| **Quantitative mindset bias on qualitative work?** | Yes (strong) |
| **Discourse community signals (editorial board)** | International child/adolescent psychiatry; ACAMH leadership |

## Strategic Notes

### Hard Blockers

- Failure to make data available on request → rejection or retraction (community evidence: ACAMH editorial policy 2026-05)
- ~50% rejection at first-week triage (community evidence: editage.com 2026-05)
- Pure qualitative work without clinical-mechanism framing
- Failure to disclose AI use
- Manuscripts outside child/adolescent psychiatry scope

### Soft Tax

Low for child-psychiatry research authors with strong methodology and data-sharing readiness. Moderate for cross-disciplinary work — must align with domain-editor structure. Data-sharing requirement is firm; submissions must be prepared for data-on-request fulfillment.

### Best Suited For

- Child and adolescent psychiatry empirical research
- Autism, ADHD, neurodevelopmental disorder studies
- Child trauma / abuse mechanism and intervention research
- Maternal mental health and perinatal psychiatry
- Treatment trials in child / adolescent mental health
- Meta-analyses of child-psychiatry literatures
- Family / caregiver dynamics research

### Not Recommended For

- Adult-only research (unless explicitly developmental-trajectory framed)
- Pure autoethnographic or first-person clinical narratives
- Critical / discursive child mental health work
- Authors without data-sharing capability
- Pure theoretical work without clinical impact

### Rejection Fallback Chain

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Developmental Psychology](./developmental-psychology.md) | If the work is more developmental-process than clinical; APA family |
| 2 | [Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology](./journal-of-consulting-and-clinical-psychology.md) | If treatment-focused and lifespan-broader; APA family |
| 3 | [Journal of Psychopathology and Clinical Science](./journal-of-psychopathology-and-clinical-science.md) | If mechanism-focused and clinical-science framing; APA family |

**Reverse direction** *(optional)*: If your paper was rejected from a top general-psychiatry venue as "too child-focused," JCPP is often a better fit because: it specializes in child + adolescent psychiatry with deep reviewer-pool expertise; domain-editor structure ensures focused review; and ACAMH affiliation provides built-in clinical audience.
